memory_candidates.content: When adding a repository-containment predicate to a git pathspec filter, resolve the pathspec's PARENT directory with realpath -m and leave the final component unresolved. Verified empirically: an in-repo leaf symlink whose target is outside the repo is a LEGAL `git add` argument (rc=0, staged as a symlink), so a leaf-resolving `realpath -m --relative-to=$ROOT -- $p` predicate classifies it as out-of-repo and drops it -- a false-positive regression. A path THROUGH an in-repo symlinked directory is fatal to git (`fatal: pathspec ... is beyond a symbolic link`) and SHOULD be dropped. The parent-resolving form (`realpath -m --relative-to=$ROOT_RESOLVED -- $(dirname -- $p)`, out-of-repo when the result is empty, `..`, or `../*`) agrees with git add's own accept/reject verdict on every pathspec shape tested, including `..`-laundered paths and a sibling directory sharing the root as a literal prefix (`<root>-backup`), which a naive string-prefix comparison gets wrong. Resolve the root through the same realpath call, never raw.

A test fixture using a real absolute out-of-repository path (e.g. /etc/passwd) as a 'genuine git-add failure' probe is fragile against any future repository-containment fix: once such a fix lands, the out-of-repo path gets classified and dropped BEFORE git add ever sees it, silently flipping the fixture's outcome from 'refuses/aborts' to 'succeeds with a warning' and defeating its original purpose. Prefer an in-repo mechanism for a 'genuine add failure' fixture instead -- e.g. a permission-denied file (chmod 000) reliably makes `git add` fail with 'fatal: adding files failed' while mixed valid paths in the same call are NOT staged either, matching the all-or-nothing hazard the fixture is meant to pin, and remains unaffected by any future out-of-repo containment logic since its parent directory never resolves outside the project root.
